tools.name: find_business
tools.description: Find businesses on ServeCounter that take bookings from assistants: by name (`query`, at least 3 letters, such as "studio noord"), by trade (`trade`, such as "barber" or "nail-salon"; the trade's key or its English or Dutch name), by place (`city`, or `latitude` and `longitude` with `radiusKm`, 10 b

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: A business's locations, services, prices, add-ons and what it asks to be paid up front, the same as its booking page shows and nothing else. Needs no sign-in. With more than one open location, answer again with its `locationId` to see its services.

tools.name: get_free_times
tools.description: The free times for one service at one location, day by day, as the booking page offers them: at most 14 days a request. Needs no sign-in. Times are in the location's own time zone.

tools.name: prepare_booking
tools.description: Prepares a booking for the person who allowed you, for a free time. Nothing is booked yet: it returns a link (`orderUrl`) to give to the person. They read who the seller is and the terms, tick two boxes and press the button, and only then is it booked. Needs the person's own ServeCounter sign-in (OA

tools.name: get_booking_status
tools.description: Where an order you prepared stands: `open` (the person has not ordered yet), `booked` (with a link to manage it) or `ended` (expired). Only for orders of the person who allowed you. Needs their sign-in.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "find_business" is 1241 chars, far longer than this server's median (248). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: prepare_booking · Public sink: prepare_booking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: prepare_booking · Public sink: prepare_booking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
